bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42521280 (elfutils): Use-of-uninitialized-value found by fuzz target fuzz-libdwfl [msan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42521280
bug_description.normalized:
The exact staged witness is a 192-byte malformed ELF64 big-endian file. In the staged vulnerable tree, libelf determines section count from `e_shoff = 0` and `e_shnum = 3`, then loads three fixed 64-byte section headers from file offset 0. Under that interpretation, section 1 is the section-header string table (`SHT_STRTAB`, `sh_offset = 8`, `sh_size = 32`) and its first string is `.debug_line_str`; section 2 has `sh_name = 0`, `sh_type = 0x6ffffff6 (SHT_GNU_HASH)`, `sh_offset = 32`, and `sh_size = 158`. In `global_read()`'s type-discovery scan, `scn_dwarf_type()` resolves `elf_strptr (result->elf, 1, 0)` for section 2 to `.debug_line_str`. Because that name starts with `.debug_` and has no `.dwo` suffix, `scn_dwarf_type()` returns `TYPE_PLAIN`, so `global_read()` promotes `result->type` to `TYPE_PLAIN`. In the later `check_section()` scan of the same section, the identical name resolution again yields `.debug_line_str`, and the `result->type == TYPE_PLAIN` guard lets libdw classify this non-string `SHT_GNU_HASH` section as the DWARF string section `IDX_debug_line_str` and request its data with `elf_getdata()`.

Inside libelf, `__libelf_set_rawdata_wrlock()` copies the section-2 header tuple into locals, maps `SHT_GNU_HASH` to `ELF_T_GNUHASH`, and on ELFCLASS64 assigns `entsize = 1`, so the non-multiple-of-word size `sh_size = 158` is accepted instead of being rejected as malformed. `__libelf_set_data_list_rdlock()` then calls `convert_data()` with `data = ELFDATA2MSB`, `size = 158`, and `type = ELF_T_GNUHASH`; because the saved x86_64 build uses `MY_ELFDATA = ELFDATA2LSB`, the fast path is skipped and `convert_data()` allocates a fresh 158-byte heap buffer before dispatching `__elf_xfctstom[ELFCLASS64 - 1][ELF_T_GNUHASH] = elf_cvt_gnuhash`.

For this exact section body, `elf_cvt_gnuhash()` swaps the first four 32-bit control words, yielding `bitmask_words = 0`, so the 64-bit loop is skipped. The trailing loop converts 35 full 32-bit words and stops with `len = 2`. In the vulnerable revision the function then falls off the end with no copy of those last two bytes, leaving `dest[156]` and `dest[157]` uninitialized even though the source section still has concrete file bytes there. `convert_data()` publishes that partially initialized heap allocation as `data->d_buf`. Back in `check_section()`, `.debug_line_str` maps to a string-section index, so the trailing-NUL trim loop runs with `size = data->d_size = 158` and first evaluates `*((const char *) data->d_buf + 157) != '\0'`. That read lands in the two-byte uninitialized tail and produces the saved MemorySanitizer report at `libdw/dwarf_begin_elf.c:265`. The fix changes the early exits in `elf_cvt_gnuhash()` to `goto done` and adds `if (len > 0) memmove (dest + size - len, src + size - len, len);`, which copies those final two bytes and removes the undefined read.

source.description: Source. During `global_read()`'s type-discovery scan, `scn_dwarf_type()` resolves the attacker-controlled section-name offset through the attacker-controlled shstrtab and materializes section 2's misleading name as `.debug_line_str`, which is the earliest project-side state that puts this non-string `SHT_GNU_HASH` section on the vulnerable DWARF path.
source.value_from: For the staged 192-byte witness, libelf accepts `shstrndx = 1`, section 1 is `SHT_STRTAB` at file offset 8 with first string `.debug_line_str`, and section 2's header carries `sh_name = 0`. This statement therefore returns the exact string `.debug_line_str` for section 2.

sink.description: MSAN sink. Because `.debug_line_str` is treated as a string section, this backward trim loop reads `data->d_buf[size - 1]`; on the saved witness the first iteration dereferences `data->d_buf[157]` from the two-byte tail that `elf_cvt_gnuhash()` never wrote.
sink.note: Both `sanitizer_trace.txt` and `reproduction_report.json` identify `check_section` at `libdw/dwarf_begin_elf.c:265:7` as the observed `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` site.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The vulnerable GNU-hash converter only writes complete 4-byte units after the control-word phase and has no fallback copy for leftover bytes. For the exact 158-byte witness, the earlier control words set `bitmask_words = 0`, this loop consumes 35 full words, and the final two bytes of the destination buffer remain uninitialized.
root_cause.note: `patch.diff` records the missing obligation precisely: it replaces the earlier `return` sites with `goto done`, tracks the original buffer length in `size`, and adds `if (len > 0) memmove (dest + size - len, src + size - len, len);` to define any remaining tail bytes.

tainted_value_origin.code: offset = shdr->sh_offset; size = shdr->sh_size; type = shdr->sh_type; align = shdr->sh_addralign; flags = shdr->sh_flags;
tainted_value_origin.description: The concrete witness-derived state that drives the conversion bug is section 2's header tuple: `sh_offset = 32`, `sh_size = 158`, `sh_type = SHT_GNU_HASH`, and `sh_addralign = 0x2020202020202020`.

parser_admitted.description: Parser admission. `gelf_getehdr()` and `elf_getshdrstrndx()` have already accepted the malformed file as ELF64 with `shstrndx = 1`, and `dwarf_begin_elf()` now enters `global_read()` to iterate every section and call `check_section()` on the misnamed `SHT_GNU_HASH` section.

coarse_trace.summary: libdw accepts the witness as an ELF file, resolves section 2's name through shstrtab section 1 as `.debug_line_str` during the type-discovery scan, promotes `result->type` to `TYPE_PLAIN`, and then the later `check_section()` pass classifies that same GNU-hash section as DWARF string data worth loading with `elf_getdata()`.

libelf materializes section 2's `sh_offset = 32`, `sh_size = 158`, and `sh_type = SHT_GNU_HASH`, accepts the odd 158-byte size on ELF64 by assigning `entsize = 1`, tags the section as `ELF_T_GNUHASH`, and allocates a 158-byte conversion buffer.

The exact GNU-hash converter swaps only full words; for this witness `bitmask_words = 0`, the trailing loop leaves `len = 2`, and the final two destination bytes remain uninitialized because the vulnerable helper has no tail copy.

The partially initialized `Elf_Data` buffer is published back to libdw, `.debug_line_str` maps to a string-section index, and the trailing-NUL trim loop reads the uninitialized last byte, triggering the saved MSAN report.

Because the section is not `SHF_COMPRESSED`, libelf classifies it by section type. `__libelf_data_type()` therefore stores `scn->rawdata.d.d_type = ELF_T_GNUHASH` for this `SHT_GNU_HASH` section.

This fast-path predicate is false. The witness file is big-endian (`ELFDATA2MSB`), the saved x86_64 build uses `MY_ELFDATA = ELFDATA2LSB`, and step 9 passed `type = ELF_T_GNUHASH`, so `convert_data()` must take the structured conversion branch instead of aliasing or byte-copying the section buffer.
MSAN allocation origin. `convert_data()` allocates a fresh 158-byte destination buffer for the converted section data, and `malloc` leaves all 158 bytes uninitialized until later writes define them.

Root cause. On the exact 158-byte section body, the earlier control-word phase stores `bitmask_words = 0`, so the 64-bit loop is skipped. This trailing loop then converts 35 full 32-bit words and exits with `len = 2`; the vulnerable function has no trailing-byte copy, so `dest[156]` and `dest[157]` stay uninitialized.

Sink. `size` is initialized from `data->d_size = 158`, so the first loop test reads `*((const char *) data->d_buf + 157)`. Step 13 left `data->d_buf[156..157]` undefined, so this first-byte check triggers the saved `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` report.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Yes. The saved MSAN trace and `reproduction_report.json` both identify `check_section` at `libdw/dwarf_begin_elf.c:265` as the crashing read, which is the exact sink anchored at fine-trace step 16.
cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Yes. MSAN attributes the poisoned bytes to the heap allocation at `convert_data:166` (fine-trace step 11), and fine-trace steps 12 through 14 show the exact `elf_cvt_gnuhash` conversion path that leaves bytes `156..157` of that allocation undefined before step 16 reads them.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved crash stack `check_section -> global_read -> dwarf_begin_elf -> load_dw -> find_dw -> dwfl_module_getdwarf -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` matches fine-trace step 16 plus the parser-admission path, and the saved allocation stack `convert_data -> __libelf_set_data_list_rdlock -> __elf_getdata_rdlock -> elf_getdata -> check_section` matches the libelf and sink portion of fine-trace steps 9 through 16.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. Step 1 materializes section 2's deceptive name `.debug_line_str`, step 3 stores `result->type = TYPE_PLAIN`, step 5 uses that state to set `cnt = IDX_debug_line_str`, step 6 imports the section's `size = 158` and `type = SHT_GNU_HASH`, step 8 stores `ELF_T_GNUHASH`, step 9 passes `ELFDATA2MSB` plus that typed 158-byte section into `convert_data()`, step 11 allocates the destination buffer, step 13 leaves the final two bytes undefined, step 14 publishes that buffer as `data->d_buf`, and step 16 reads `data->d_buf[157]` in the string-tail scan.

poc.trigger: Stage 01 reproduced the crash by running `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_42521280 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which produced `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` in `check_section` at `libdw/dwarf_begin_elf.c:265`.

format.name: malformed ELF64 big-endian file
format.contract: The available evidence establishes only the exact staged 192-byte witness and the concrete layout libelf derives from it. In the vulnerable parser path, libelf uses `e_shoff = 0`, `e_shnum = 3`, and fixed 64-byte section headers; section 1 is `SHT_STRTAB` at file offset 8 with first string `.debug_line_str`, and section 2 has `sh_name = 0`, `sh_type = SHT_GNU_HASH`, `sh_offset = 32`, and `sh_size = 158`. `scn_dwarf_type()` resolves section 2 as `.debug_line_str`, `global_read()` promotes `result->type` to `TYPE_PLAIN`, and the later `check_section()` pass therefore treats the section as `.debug_line_str`; `elf_getdata()` then converts its 158 bytes through `elf_cvt_gnuhash`, and the vulnerable helper leaves the last two bytes undefined before the backward trailing-NUL scan reads `data->d_buf[157]`. The staged artifacts do not justify a broader class of ELF files or all GNU-hash sections.
